methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional capacity-building outside metro hubs, creating potential for distributed AI fluency through accessible workforce training—a critical test of whether deep capability can spread beyond NoVA and Richmond.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA signals deliberate community-driven AI education infrastructure in Virginia's second-tier metro, potentially creating a replicable model for distributed deep capability rather than platform-dependent shallow adoption.

signals.title: New Jersey, Virginia Can Lead the Nation By Building ‘AI Resilience Cohorts’ to Develop Early-Career, State Talent Pipelines - Federation of American Scientists
signals.signal_reading: The AI Resilience Cohorts proposal explicitly targets state-led talent pipeline development, representing a policy framework that could distribute deep AI capability across regions rather than concentrating it in existing tech hubs—a structural intervention against the widening gap.

signals.title: Residents share data center concerns with state senators during listening tour stop in Danville
signals.signal_reading: Danville residents voicing data center concerns without apparent local capability-building signals infrastructure extraction rather than distributed AI economy participation—economic activity concentrated elsewhere while communities bear costs without skill development or opportunity access.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: NBC's feature on NoVA residents questioning who benefits from the AI boom reveals deepening concentration dynamics—infrastructure and capital amassing in data center capital while questioning local capability distribution suggests excellence consolidating rather than spreading.
